title: Selvage Session Protocol — version and capability negotiation
description: The parts of `selvage/1` that decide whether two peers can talk at all: the wire version grammar, the compatibility rule, capability names, and the advertised block (`capabilities` plus `keepalive`) that both `GET /meta` and the reply to `session.hello` carry. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §10; the canonical byte form is CANONICAL.md §2.5.

wireVersion.description: A wire version a receiver must accept as syntactically well formed: `selvage/` then a major, then optionally a minor. Leading zeros are not part of the grammar. The compatibility rule is separate: same major, and while at 0.x also the same minor (§10). `selvage/1`, `selvage/1.0` and `selvage/1.9` are all this implementation's version.

canonicalWireVersion.description: A wire version as a conforming producer writes it: `selvage/1` for the version the reference server speaks, never `selvage/1.0`. The minor is written only when it is not zero, because zero is the default (CANONICAL.md §2.5).

capabilityName.description: A capability name. Unknown names are ignored by both sides and there is no failure mode for one a peer cannot honour (§10; `NOTES.md` §B.9); there is therefore no schema that says a capability is mandatory.

keepalive.description: The session's clocks, advertised by the server. The advertised values are the session's: a client that substitutes its own disagrees with its peers about when a cursor is stale (§8.2, §9). `/meta`'s object carries `room_grace_ms` in addition to the three clocks the handshake reply also carries.

awareness_expire_ms.description: How long a client keeps a remote awareness state it has not seen renewed. A state not renewed inside this window will be forgotten, and the forgetting happens on the renewal tick, so it can arrive up to `awareness_renew_ms` late (§8.2).

awareness_renew_ms.description: How often a client republishes its own awareness state.

ping_interval_ms.description: How often the server sends a WebSocket Ping. Protocol-level pings are not session messages and are never relayed (§9).

room_grace_ms.description: The server's default room grace period: how long a room survives its host disconnecting. Advertised in `GET /meta`'s `keepalive` (§2), and carried per room as `grace_ms` in `host.detached` (§9). A client reads it to size its reconnect retry so that it does not give up inside a window the room still exists for (§9.1); the number is policy. In `selvage/2` the same number is how long a room survives its **last** connection ending rather than its host's, and `/meta` is where a client of that version reads it (PROTOCOL.md §1.2, §2).

advertisedVersions.description: The versions a server accepts, in `GET /meta`. Empty is not a valid advertisement: a server that accepts nothing has no reason to answer.

capabilityList.description: An advertised capability list. Advertised additively and read additively: a peer ignores names it does not know, in `/meta` and in the handshake reply.
